start_with: Confirm the installed Rock version is 14 or later.
Confirm the exact TV application exists under Apple TV Apps.
Inspect its generated Start Screen and default-page configuration.
Render the page’s Lava and verify that the result is valid TVML.
Confirm the testing shell points to the intended application rather than compiled or stale demo settings.
Inspect the page cacheability setting.
Stop when resolution requires changing the shell package or an unverified production setting.
branches.title: The application or Start Screen does not load
branches.when: The application or Start Screen does not load

do_not_assume: If the same markup works in another template, do not assume equivalence; compare each template’s supported structure.
start_with: Inspect the final TVML after Lava rendering, not only the stored template.
Confirm that the selected template accepts the elements being emitted.
Check Lava conditions involving `CurrentPerson`, `Context`, or page parameters.
Remove assumptions based on HTML, browser CSS, SVG, or WebView behavior.
Test the page in both Light and Dark themes.
If the same markup works in another template, do not assume equivalence; compare each template’s supported structure.
branches.title: A page is blank, malformed, or rejected
branches.when: A page is blank, malformed, or rejected

start_with: Confirm that the external Rock page contains a Remote Authentication block.
Confirm that the block is associated with the intended TV application site.
Confirm that the application’s Authentication Page points to that external page.
Confirm that the login command references the intended login, timeout, and success pages.
Confirm the page uses the case-sensitive `{ authQrCodeUrl }` and `{ authCode }` fields with single braces.
Confirm the person is authenticated on the external Rock site.
If the current installation follows the inspected source implementation, investigate code lifetime and device-identifier matching.
Stop before exposing authentication session records or identifiers in public diagnostics.
branches.title: Login shows no QR code or manual code
branches.when: Login shows no QR code or manual code

start_with: Inspect `rockLoginClearNavigationStack`.
Inspect `rockLogoutClearNavigationStack`.
Unless the journey requires otherwise, retain the documented default of `true`.
Test Back navigation after successful login, timeout, logout, and failed authentication.
Verify the success and logout destination pages.
branches.title: Back navigation exposes the pre-login or personalized page unexpectedly
branches.when: Back navigation exposes the pre-login or personalized page unexpectedly

start_with: Confirm the command is `playVideo` or `playAudio`.
Confirm video uses a direct MP4 or HLS source.
Confirm audio uses a direct MP3 source.
Reject YouTube as a supported source for these commands.
Inspect the exact media URL and metadata parameters.
If Rock watch tracking is expected, inspect the Media Element and related-entity parameters.
Test the same media without interaction parameters to separate playback failure from tracking failure.
branches.title: Video or audio does not play
branches.when: Video or audio does not play

start_with: Determine whether the intended outcome is resume only, append to an existing interaction, or create a new interaction from a prior position.
For resume position, inspect `rockWatchMap`.
To append progress, verify both `rockWatchMap` and `rockInteractionGuid`.
If a new interaction is intended, omit `rockInteractionGuid`.
Inspect whether resume has been explicitly disabled.
Retest with a known prior stopping point.
branches.title: Playback resumes incorrectly or creates duplicate interactions
branches.when: Playback resumes incorrectly or creates duplicate interactions

do_not_assume: Do not treat a reference-gallery screenshot as proof that TVML can reproduce the layout.
start_with: Determine whether the page follows the system theme or declares its own.
Inspect Light and Dark media-query branches.
Check foreground colors, badge tint, image contrast, and text shadows in both themes.
Keep shadows close to text if vertical clipping occurs.
Do not treat a reference-gallery screenshot as proof that TVML can reproduce the layout.
branches.title: Colors or badges disappear in one theme
branches.when: Colors or badges disappear in one theme

start_with: Confirm the asset is an LCR file.
Confirm the image source is a direct link to that file.
Reject an LSR file for this workflow.
For app icons, confirm three separate layers with PNG foregrounds and a JPG background.
Confirm the dimensions for the intended @1x, @2x, or App Store use.
For shell-embedded resources, remove the file extension from the resource name.
branches.title: A parallax image is flat or missing
branches.when: A parallax image is flat or missing

start_with: Confirm the shell points to the intended application.
Inspect the page’s cacheability type.
Confirm whether demo settings or compiled settings are active.
Restart the application when using the documented demo-key workflow.
Use `clearDemo` only when the intended outcome is to restore compiled settings.
Make a controlled cacheability change only after confirming that freshness, not malformed TVML, is the issue.
branches.title: A template change does not appear
branches.when: A template change does not appear

start_with: Confirm the shell was compiled with demo-mode support.
Use `showDemo` to enter the documented demo screen.
Use `updateDemo` only within that screen.
Confirm the demo key and restart flow.
Use `clearDemo` to return to compiled settings.
Stop if the demo service or Rock Core application is no longer available; current availability requires separate verification.
branches.title: Demo commands do not work

start_with: Inspect `completedCommand`.
Inspect `completedCommandSecondThreshold`.
Determine how many seconds remained when the control initialized.
Provide a completed panel even when a completion command is present.
Test initial loads immediately before and after the target time.
branches.title: A countdown immediately navigates or starts media
branches.when: A countdown immediately navigates or starts media

start_with: Identify the exact Lava Webhook Defined Value matched by the request URL and verb.
Inspect the complete template output.
Inventory every enabled Lava command.
Verify the protection mechanism independently; Rock documents no default webhook security.
Remove unnecessary data and commands before considering the endpoint ready.
Stop immediately if person or other sensitive data is reachable without the intended control.
branches.title: A Lava webhook exposes more data than expected
branches.when: A Lava webhook exposes more data than expected

entrypoint: Choose the branch whose symptom matches the user's task, then inspect the live records before making changes.
